title: Free Sewing
content: **List of Contents** Free Sewing Create Free Sewing Directional Notch **Free Sewing** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QQe_bw0nfyQ \- Freely create Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Lines. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022454888/mceclip0.png) **Free Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Sewing ▶ **Free Sewing** ** Create Free Sewing** \- Four clicks are needed to create a pair of Free Sewing Lines. * **Freehand Sewing** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eIvkBJG8oRU \- Navigate to the 2D window and hover over the Pattern outline or the Internal Line where the Sewing Line should be created. A blue point will follow along the mouse cursor. \- Click on the Pattern outline or the Internal Line to start the Sewing Line. Drag the mouse cursor to designate the direction. Then, click again to complete the first half of the Sewing Line. \- Create the second half of the Sewing Line as above. When click and dragging the mouse cursor after establishing the start point, a blue point will appear to guide the length of the first half of the Sewing Line. Click again to complete the second half of the Sewing Line. * **Create Sewing with Designated Value** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N-CeRmJwUMY \- While click and dragging the mouse cursor after establishing the start point, right-click to access the create Sewing Line window. \- Type in the desired value and select OK. \- When the length of the Sewing Line is designated, the end point of the Sewing Line will be created automatically. **Directional Notch** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=697F-APCrRo \- The Directional Notch’s position alters depending on the movement of the mouse cursor. \- To reset the Directional Notch of the first half of the Sewing, you must cancel the action and restart. \- To cancel the first half of the Sewing Line, hit the Esc key or the Ctrl+Z keys on the keyboard. \- To reset the Directional Notch of the second half, cancel the action before creating the end point and recreate the Sewing Line. \- To cancel the second half of the Sewing Line, hit the Delete key or the Backspace key on the keyboard. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive guidance and video tutorials on using the Free Sewing tool, including techniques for freehand sewing and creating sewing lines with designated values.

title: Edit Curve Point
content: **List of Contents** Edit Curve Point Edit Free Curve Points Add Free Curve Points to Free Curves Delete Free Curve Points **Edit Curve Point** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FdD7RphLY58 \- Add and edit free curve points on segments. \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021960108/mceclip0.png) **Edit Curve point** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Curve Point.** ** Edit Free Curve Points YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZJrsmbhhtAU** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021960108/mceclip0.png) **Edit Curve Point** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window and click on a segment to add a curve point. \- Click and drag the added curve point to edit the curvature. \- Or, click and drag the segment to add and edit the curvature simultaneously. \- Select and move multiple Curve Points at once. While moving the Curve Points, right click to type in desired Distance Moved (ver.4.2.0). **Add Free Curve Points to Free Curves** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8YwBvZSuZDE \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021960108/mceclip0.png) **Edit Curve Point** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- When a curve point is added to a free curve, the curve will be modified based on the added curve point. **Delete Free Curve Points YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AO6Zi9xpGRo ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021960108/mceclip0.png) **Edit Curve Point** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Select the curve point and hit the Delete key on the keyboard. \- The selected curve point will be deleted. \- Select and delete multiple Curve Points at once(ver.4.2.0). Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for users to effectively edit, add, and delete free curve points within a 2D pattern design.

title: Offset as Internal Line along Curve
content: **List of Contents** Offset as Internal Line along Curve Number of Offsets Offset Distance to Segment Edge Straight Line Perpendicular Direction **Offset as Internal Line along Curve** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wrdsfSxb8gM \- Create Internal Lines between two Pattern outlines along their curve. \- Select two lines and right click to access the pop-up menu. Then, select **Offset as Internal Line along Curve.** \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447008/mceclip0.png) **Edit Pattern** tool, select two lines which Internal Lines will offset In between. Then, right-click and select **Offset as Internal Line along Curve.** \- The Offset as Internal Line along Curve window will appear. ** Number of Offsets** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqyGtECwN10 \- Set how many Internal Lines will be created in between the selected lines. **Offset** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RWu6SUTyxQk \- Set the distance between the offset Internal Lines. **Distance to Segment Edge** \- Set how far the offset Internal Lines will apart from the Pattern outline. * **Reverse Direction ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OzXu1UKPEXc \- Horizontally reverse the Internal Lines’ position based on the Di"stance to Segment Edge. * **Opposite Segment** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=op3Z5EWxzUo \- Vertically reverse the Internal Lines’ position based on the Distance to Segment Edge. **Straight Line** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P-tELnIhKJQ \- Create offset Internal Lines as straight lines. **Perpendicular Direction** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OnggOP95HfM \- The offset Internal Lines will be created perpendicular to the Pattern outlines. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for creating and manipulating internal lines along curves in pattern design, featuring instructional videos and step-by-step instructions for various offset options.

title: Invert Selection
content: **Invert Selection** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9eR9epYrw0Y \- Invert the Pattern selection, selecting the Patterns currently not selected. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021445568/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021388307/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window and right click on the desired Pattern to select Invert Selection from the pop-up menu. \- The selection will be inverted, selecting the ones that are not currently selected.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on how to use the "Invert Selection" feature in Clo3D to easily select unselected patterns within your design workspace.

title: [Property] Create Button Texture
content: ### **Objective** Create and apply custom textures to buttons in CLO in order to express various button styles. * UV maps for each default button are included in the CLO Asset Library as photoshop files. * The files can be opened and edited in Adobe Photoshop to apply custom textures and logos to the existing button shapes. * When UV maps are used, all images or type will increase or decrease in size when the button width, ligne, or thickness are changed in CLO. **Operation** 1. Download UV maps of buttons from the [Library window](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000527827-Library-Window). ![Button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360081953953/Button.png) 2. Locate the asset folder on your computer. (**PC:** C:\Users\Public\Documents\CLO\Assets / **MAC:** User/Library/Application Support/CLO) **※ Note:** on PC you can right click on the folder name in CLO Library and choose “Copy the path”. Then you can paste this path location into a file browser to locate it. 3. Open .psd file in Adobe Photoshop. There are 4 types of layouts that UV maps will have. ![UV.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360081938953/UV.png) 4. Each part has a separate layer with a shape defining the section that needs to be filled or covered. 5. An image can be placed/embedded or a pattern [Define](https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/using/creating-patterns.html) and filled to cover the desired location. Type can allose be added. 6. Hide UV outlines and Text layers, then save the image. **※ Note:** Saving the image in .jpeg format is recommended. 7. Open the custom saved UV map through the Texture section of the[ button property](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115006020988--Style-Property-Apply-Custom-Button-Texture).
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating and applying custom textures to buttons in CLO, enabling users to personalize button styles using UV maps and Adobe Photoshop.

title: Guide for Installing Network Version in the Same Network Envrionment
content: **List of Contents** Guideline for Installing Network Version in the Same Network Environment 1\. Check-up on HASP Driver Installation on Server PC 2\. Additional Set-up ACC Page on Client PC **Guide for Installing Network Version in the same Network Environment** **Objective** Install Network version in the same Network Environment when Server (PC connected to the red HASP Key) is unable to recognize Client (PC to run the software). **1\. Check-up on HASP Driver Installation on Server PC** **Operation** 1. Access to the Web Browser: [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/) Check Sentinel HASP Driver is installed and operating on Server as shown in the image below. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000737867/sever_1.png) 2. If the web page does not appear, reinstall Sentinel HASP Driver. [HASP Driver Install Guide ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115000558507) **2\. Additional Set-up ACC Page on Client** **Operation** 1. Set up ACC page on PC you want to run the software. 2. ACC Page : [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/) 3. Click on **Configuration** (the red box in the image below). ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000737927/page_add_1.jpg) 4. Click **Access to Remote License Managers**. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000785928/page_add_2.jpg) 5. Check on 'Aggressive Search for Remote Licenses' (image below) and type the Server PC IP in "Specify Search Parameters" then click **Submit**. **※ Note:** **How to check your IP:** Windows Search ▶ Search 'Cmd.exe' ▶ Type 'ipconfig' <http://www.ghacks.net/2011/05/17/network-troubleshooting-basics-the-ipconfig-command/>[ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000737907/page_add_3.jpg) ](http://www.ghacks.net/2011/05/17/network-troubleshooting-basics-the-ipconfig-command/) 6. Wait for 10 seconds and its completed when HASP key page shows up (image below). If the page does not show up, the Server and Client may possibly be connected to different network environment. In that case, follow the link below, follow the guideline and try again. [Guideline for Installing Network Version on the Internet Environment ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115000617048-%EC%9D%B8%ED%84%B0%EB%84%B7-%ED%99%98%EA%B2%BD%EC%97%90%EC%84%9C-Network-%EB%B2%84%EC%A0%84-%EC%84%A4%EC%B9%98-%EB%B0%A9%EB%B2%95) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000737887/page_add_4.png) Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for installing the network version of software in the same network environment, ensuring proper recognition of clients by the server.

title: Show/Hide Bond/Skive
content: ### **Objective** Show or hide bonded or skived area in the 3D window (ver2.3.0). **Location** Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 3D Trims ▶ **Show Bond/Skive** (ver4.2 or earlier) 3D Trims Display Icon ▶ **Show Bond/Skive** (ver4.2 or earlier) Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 3D Trims ▶ **Show Bond/Skive**(ver5.0 or later) 3D Window ▶ 3D Trims Display Icon ▶ **Show Bond/Skive** (ver5.0 or later) **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below:** ** 3D Trims Display Icon ▶ **Show Bond/Skive** → The selected area's bond/skive in the 3D window is now being shown or hidden.

title: [Object Browser] Delete Button Style
content: ### **Objective** Delete unnecessary button styles. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Button Tab **Operation ** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Tab 2. Select a button style to be deleted. 3. Press Delete on keyboard or right click on the button style and select **Delete** option. → The selected button style is not deleted.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for deleting unnecessary button styles in the Object Browser's Button Tab.

title: [2D Tool] M:N Segment Sewing
content: **Objective** Easily sew multiple segments (M) to multiple segments (N) at once and edit them as a group. When the total length of multiple segments corresponding to M is different from the total length of multiple segments corresponding to N, N segments are divided in proportion to M segments. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **M:N Segment Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001290748/M_N________.png) **M:N Segment Sewing** **※ Note:** Hold down the **Segment Sewing** tool for a while to access the **M:N Segment Sewing** tool. ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **M:N Segment Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001290748/M_N________.png) **M:N Segment Sewing** 2. Click on the segments belong to M segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M sewing lines. → M sewing lines are highlighted in neon color. 3. As checking the Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on N segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. → The Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. **※ Note:** * While establishing M:N sewing lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. * When you click on an inappropriate segment while sewing, the segment appears in red and you cannot establish Sewing Line on the selected segment. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: The M:N Segment Sewing page provides a streamlined process for simultaneously sewing and editing multiple segments, ensuring proportional adjustments when segment lengths differ.

title: Reset 3D Arrangement
content: ### **Objective** Return arrangement of the entire or selected Patterns back to pre-simulation state in the 3D window. Use this function when draping does not operate properly after arranging around the Avatar. ** Location** **Selected Pattern** 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ **Reset 3D Arrangement (Selected)** ****All Pattern**** Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Reset 3D Arrangement (All)** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001244168/_________________.png) **Reset 3D Arrangement (All)** ** Operation** **Selected Pattern** 1. Select a 3D Pattern to reset its arrangement. **※ Note:** Press Shift key on keyboard to select multiple Patterns. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ **Reset 3D Arrangement (Selected)** → The selected Pattern is now being rearranged back to pre-simulation state. **All Pattern** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Reset 3D Arrangement (All)** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001244168/_________________.png) **Reset 3D Arrangement (All)** → The entire Pattern is now being rearranged back to pre-simulation state.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for resetting the arrangement of selected or all patterns in the 3D window back to their pre-simulation state to resolve draping issues.

title: Rotate
content: **List of Contents** Rotate Clockwise/Counterclockwise X/Y Axis Parallel To **Objective** Rotate Patterns and Internal Shapes/Lines based on various references. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern** / **Edit Pattern** ** **2D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001097387/1.png) **Transform Pattern** / ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001143808/2.png) **Edit Pattern** ** Operation** **Rotate** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern** / **Edit Pattern** ** **2D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001097387/1.png) **Transform Pattern** / ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001143808/2.png) **Edit Pattern** 2. Select the Pattern or Internal Shapes/ Lines or Baselines to be rotated. → The marquee box appears around the selected item. 3. Click and drag the rotate point on top of the marquee box. → The selected item rotates towards the mouse. **※ Note:** * While clicking and dragging the Pattern, Internal Shapes/Lines, or Baselines, right click to access the Rotate window. Type in the desired angle, then click OK. The selected item rotates based on the entered value (ver3.2.0). **Clockwise/Counterclockwise** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern** / **Edit Pattern** ** **2D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001097387/1.png) **Transform Pattern** / ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001143808/2.png) **Edit Pattern ** 2. Click on the Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines to be rotated. Then, right click to access the pop-up menu. 3. When the pop-up menu appears, select **Clockwise (45º)** or **Clockwise (90º)** or **Counterclockwise (45º)** or **Counterclockwise (90º)** → The selected pattern rotates according to the chosen options. **X/Y Axis** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern** / **Edit Pattern** ** **2D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001097387/1.png) **Transform Pattern** / ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001143808/2.png) **Edit Pattern**** ** 2. Click on the Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines to be rotated. Then, right click to access the pop-up menu. 3. When the pop-up menu appears, select **X-Axis** or **Y-Axis**. 4. Select the line of a Pattern which should be rotated to the chosen axis. → The selected Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines are rotated to X-Axis or Y-Axis on the basis of the selected line. **Parallel To** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern** / **Edit Pattern** ** **2D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001097387/1.png) **Transform Pattern** / ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001143808/2.png) **Edit Pattern**** ** 2. Click on the Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines to be rotated. Then, right click to access the pop-up menu. 3. When the pop-up menu appears, select **Parallel to... ** 4. Select the line of any Patterns or Internal Lines/Shapes in the 2D window which the previously selected Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines are rotated to. This line acts as a fiducial line. → The selected line turns red. 5. Then, select the line of the rotating Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines that will rotate parallel to the fiducial line selected above. → The Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines rotates parallel to the fiducial line. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for rotating 2D patterns and internal shapes or lines using various techniques in the editing tool.

title: Align Points
content: **Objective** Align multiple points along specific direction or axes (ver2.3.0). ** Location** Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Points) ▶ **Left / Center / Right / Top / Middle / Bottom / To Point (X-Axis) / To Point (Y-Axis)** ** Operation** 1. Navigate to 2D toolbar and select the ![2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115001011307/2.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. 2. Select more than two points to be aligned. 3. Right click on the fiducial point and follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Points) ▶ **Left / Center / Right / Top / Middle / Bottom / To Point (X-Axis) / To Point (Y-Axis)** →The selected points are aligned according to the selected option.
content_description: This webpage provides instructions for aligning multiple points along specific axes using the Right Click Pop-Up Menu in the 2D toolbar of the Edit Pattern tool.

title: Move with Arrow Keys (3D)
content: **List of Contents** Move Patterns with Arrow Keys Set Specific Movement Increment **Objective** Select Patterns in the 3D window, then use the arrow keys on the keyboard to move them in specific increments. ** Location** **Move Patterns with Arrow Keys ** Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Select/Move ** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024342428/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** **Set Specific Movement Increment ** Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ Grid Properties ▶ Property Editor ▶ 3D Grid ▶ **3D Arrow Key Movement** Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D/2D Window) ▶ Grid Properties ▶ Property Editor ▶ 3D Grid ▶ **3D Arrow Key Movement** **Operation** **Move Patterns with Arrow Keys** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Select/Move ** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024342428/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** ** ** 2. Select Patterns or trims in the 3D window. → Selected Patterns or trims are highlighted in yellow. 3. Use the arrow keys on the keyboard to move the selected Pattern or trim. **Arrow Keys** | **Description** ---|--- ▲ | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the positive y-axis. The Garment moves upwards. ▼ | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the negative y-axis. The Garment moves downwards. ◀ | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the negative x-axis. The Garment moves to the left. ▶ | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the positive x-axis. The Garment moves to the right. **▲ + Ctrl** | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the negative z-axis. The Garment moves away from you. **▼ + Ctrl** | Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the positive z-axis. The Garment moves towards you. **Set Specific Movement Increment** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ Grid Properties ▶ Property Editor ▶ **3D Arrow Key Movement** Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Grid Properties ▶ Property Editor ▶ **3D Arrow Key Movement** 2. Enter the desired distance moved with each arrow key input. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for using arrow keys to move selected patterns in a 3D garment design environment while allowing users to set specific movement increments.

title: Sublayer
content: **List of Contents** Set Sublayer Apply Sublayer Definition of Sublayer Delete Sublayer **Set Sublayer** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=31nAYIuA1OE \- Assign the order of patterns in layers. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022801308/mceclip0.png) **Set Sublayer** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ **Set Sublayer.** ** Apply Sublayer** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RtqT2gKcd-U \- When the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022801308/mceclip0.png) **Set Sublayer** tool is selected, all Pattern texture will disappear in the 2D window. \- Click on the Pattern as it will be highlighted in red. \- Move the cursor as the red arrow follows along the mouse cursor. \- Click on the other Pattern. \- Navigate to the 3D window and activate the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022802108/mceclip1.png) **Simulation.** \- The Pattern that was clicked at the first time will be arranged above the Pattern that was clicked at the second time. **Definition of Sublayer** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_fnS2V0WnkU \- The plus sign on the line connecting two selected Patterns indicates that the Pattern selected second will be placed above the Pattern selected first. \- Click the plus sign to change it to a minus sign. \- The minus sign indicates that the Pattern selected second will be placed below the Pattern selected first. **Delete Sublayer** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sMqqNqIZcYA \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022801308/mceclip0.png) **Set Sublayer** tool activated, click on the arrow connecting two selected Patterns. \- When the arrow is highlighted in yellow, hit the Delete key on the keyboard. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide to understanding and managing sublayers in 2D pattern design, featuring step-by-step instructions and helpful video tutorials for setting, applying, defining, and deleting sublayers.

title: Surface Circumference Measurement
content: **List of Contents** Surface Circumference Measurement Measure Circumference **Surface Circumference Measurement** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E2C1ui2zrmI \- Measure circumference of the Avatar, such as chest circumference and waist circumference, by going over the curves of the Avatar’s surface. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022742627/mceclip0.png) **Surface Circumference Measurement** tool from the 3D Toolbar or navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022742627/mceclip0.png) **Surface Circumference Measurement.** ** Measure Circumference** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_7r9jSlNbr8 \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022742627/mceclip0.png) **Surface circumference Measurement** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Click total of three times to create a Circumference Measurement. \- Click on the Avatar to create a start point of the circumference. \- Move and click on the Avatar again to decide the direction of the circumference. 。 \- Lastly, hover the mouse over the line connecting the start and second point to decide the angle of the circumference. \- When the desired circumference is achieved, click to complete. \- Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard when creating the second and the third point to move the mouse in a straight line. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on using the Surface Circumference Measurement tool to accurately measure the dimensions of an Avatar in a 3D environment.

title: Delete Line
content: **Delete Line** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dk3YaUaYH_k \- Delete a line from the 2D Window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021855567/mceclip0.png)**Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D Toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D Window, right click on a line to be deleted and select **DELETE LINE.** \- The selected line will be deleted.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on how to delete a line from the 2D Window in Clo3D using the Edit Pattern tool.

title: Linear Avatar Tape
content: **List of Contents** Linear Avatar Tape Create Tape Create Tape in Guidelines **Linear Avatar Tape** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IQhfRlenVv0 \- Apply Linear Avatar Tapes to Avatars in the 3D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022403087/mceclip2.png) **Linear Avatar Tape** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate the Main Menu and select Avatar ▶ Avatar Tape ▶ **Linear Avatar Tape.** ** Create Tape** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bMj3gXVk6Ig \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022403087/mceclip2.png) **Linear Avatar Tape** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Click to create the start point of the Avatar Tape on the Avatar. A blue dot will be created. \- Drag the mouse towards the direction the tape will be applied to and click to create the second point. A blue dot will appear as well. \- Double click where the tape should be completed. The Avatar Tape will be created and highlighted in yellow. **Create Tape in Guidelines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v7a9KgobOk8?rel=0 \- To create an Avatar Tape in guidelines, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and click to create the start point. \- Keep holding down the Shift key and click to establish the second point. \- Double click where the tape should be completed. The Avatar Tape will be created and highlighted in yellow. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for applying and creating Linear Avatar Tapes in a 3D environment, complete with instructional videos and step-by-step instructions.

title: Show 3D Pen (Avatar)
content: ### **Objective** Show or hide lines and shapes created on an Avatar as needed. ** Location** 3D Window ▶ ![_______.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015216407/_______.png) Avatar Display ▶ ![_________.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015297048/_________.png)**Show 3D Pen (Avatar)** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Window ▶ ![_______.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015216407/_______.png) Avatar Display ▶ ![_________.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015297048/_________.png) **Show 3D Pen (Avatar)** → All lines and shapes on the Avatar appears or hides. **※ Note:** When the Avatar is hidden, the lines and shapes are hidden as well.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on how to toggle the visibility of lines and shapes on an Avatar within a 3D window.

title: Convert to Baseline
content: ### **Objective** Convert Internal Lines to Baselines to utilize them as guidelines. ### **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115008327888/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) **Transform Pattern** ### **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below:** **Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶**Transform Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115008327888/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) **Transform Pattern**** ** 2. Select Internal Lines/Shapes to be converted to Baselines. → The selected Internal Lines/Shapes are highlighted in yellow. 3. Right click on the selected Internal Lines/Shapes. → The right click pop-up menu appears. 4. Select **Convert to Baseline**. → The selected Internal Lines/Shapes are converted to Baselines and they appear as purple.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for converting internal lines to baselines in Clo3D, enabling users to effectively utilize them as guidelines for pattern editing.

title: [2D Tool] 1:N Free Sewing
content: **Objective ** Freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines to sew multiple Patterns to a single Pattern (ver2.2.0). ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶**Free Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001244107/_______.png) **Free Sewing** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Free Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001244107/_______.png) **Free Sewing** 2. Establish the start and the end point on the Pattern outline, which is called as 1, where multiple Patterns are sewn to. 3. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard. → The Sewing Line appears in neon color. 4. While holding down the Shift key, establish Sewing Lines on N Patterns. Similar to setting regular Free Sewing Lines, be careful with Directional Notches. 5. Release the Shift key to complete. **※ Note** * While establishing 1:N Sewing Lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the Sewing Line cannot be applied. * While establishing N Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a step-by-step guide for users to freely establish sewing lines on pattern outlines and internal shapes, enabling the sewing of multiple patterns to a single pattern in CLO 3D.

title: [Object Browser] Apply Button Style
content: **List of Contents** Apply Button Style In Property Editor Select A Button And Apply Button Style Select A Button And Apply A New Button Style Apply a Button Style by Drag-and-Drop **Objective** Apply button styles onto buttons as desired. **Location** Object Browser ▶ **Button Tab** **Operation** **Apply Button Style In Property Editor** 1. Click on a button and select a button style in the Property Editor. → The selected button style is now being applied to the button. **Select A Button And Apply Button Style** 1. Select a button. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005601167/property_btn_assign_none.png) **Assigned to Selected Patterns** ** **→ The button style is now being applied to the selected button. **Select A Button And Apply A New Button Style** 1. Select a button. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005601187/__._______.__________________.png) **Assigned to New Fabric** → A new buttonhole style is now being added to the buttonhole list window and applied at the same time. **Apply A Button Style by Drag-and-Drop ** 1. Drag and drop a new button style onto a button in the 3D Window. → A new button style is now being added to the selected button. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for applying various button styles to buttons using the Property Editor and drag-and-drop methods.

title: [Popup] Add Point to Pattern on Start/End
content: **Objective** Add point to Pattern outline on start or end point of a Sewing line. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Edit Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005458227/________.png) **Edit Sewing** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Edit Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005458227/________.png) **Edit Sewing** 2. Right click on the Sewing Line. → The right click pop-up menu appears. 3. At your need, add point to Pattern outline on either the start or the end point of the selected Sewing Line. → The point is added respective to the chosen option. **※Note:** The point is added to the Pattern outline where the selected Sewing Line is placed on. To add point to Pattern outline where the other half Sewing Line is placed, please repeat the same procedure above.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for adding points to the pattern outline at the start or end of a sewing line in the Clo3D software.

title: [Tool] Fasten/Unfasten Button
content: **List of Contents** Fasten Button Unfasten Button ### **Objective** Fasten or unfasten buttons to style the Garment as desired. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶**Fasten Button** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005615767/________.png) **Fasten Button** **Operation** **Fasten Button** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶**Fasten Button** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005615767/________.png) **Fasten Button** 2. Click on a button, then click on its corresponding buttonhole in either the 2D or 3D environment, then continue on to the remaining buttons and buttonholes. → The buttons move above the buttonholes. → Lock icons next to the 3D buttons and buttonholes appear (ver2.5.0). **Unfasten Button** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶**Fasten Button** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005615767/________.png) **Fasten Button****** **** 2. Click on fastened buttons and buttonholes in either the 2D or 3D environment. → Buttons are now unfastened and return to their previous location. → Lock icons next to the 3D buttons and buttonholes disappear (ver2.5.0). **※ Note: ** * To fasten multiple buttons and buttonholes at once, click and drag in the 2D window to select all buttons to be fastened, then click the first buttonhole to be paired with the buttons (ver4.0.0). * To unlock multiple buttons and buttonholes, click and drag on all fastened buttons and buttonholes. * Fastened buttons and buttonholes can now be [moved](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115013407668) (ver4.0.0). Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for fastening and unfastening buttons on garments within the 2D and 3D environments of the CLO 3D software.

title: [Tool] Select/Move Button
content: **List of Contents** Move Buttons with Click-and-Drag Move Buttons with Distance Input ### Objective Move buttons as desired. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Select/Move Button** 3D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001311647/____________.png) **Select/Move Button** **Operation** **Move Buttons with Click-and-Drag** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Select/Move Button** 3D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001311647/____________.png) **Select/Move Button**** ** 2. Click and drag the buttons to the desired location on either of 2D or 3D Pattern. → The selected buttons are now being moved accordingly. **Move Buttons with Distance Input (ver2.5.0)** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Select/Move Button** 3D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001311647/____________.png) **Select/Move Button** 2. While click and dragging the buttons with left-click mouse button, click right-click mouse button in either of 2D or 3D window. → The Moving Distance window appears. **※ Note:** For the Mac OS version, click a Control key or F1 key. 3. Enter desired value in the menu. **Distance Moved** | Sets the moved distance of the buttonhole from its original location. ---|--- **Position** | Sets the position of the center of the buttonhole from the **left** /**right** /**top** /**bottom** of the Pattern outline. 4. Click **OK**. → The buttonholes are now being moved according to the input value. ** ※ Note: ** * It is able to select and move multiple buttons at once in the 2D window (ver2.4.0). * The Gizmo for **Select/Move Button** tool has been changed from 2D rotation Gizmo to 3D translocation Gizmo (ver3.1.0). ** ** Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for moving buttons in a design software using both click-and-drag and distance input methods.

title: [3D Tool] Tack on Garment
content: ### **Objective** Use this function to visualize fit adjustments by tacking temporarily. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ **Tack** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001106827/____.png)**Tack** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ **Tack** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001106827/____.png)**Tack** 2. Click on an initial point on a draped Garment. → A point is now being created with a dotted line following. 3. Click on an end point. → Another point is now being created with a yellow highlighted line. → Same tack is now being created in the 2D Pattern. 4. Activate**![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001106847/_______.png) Simulate**. → The Garment is now being simulated while the two points are being fixed to each other. **※ Note:** It is also available to create and modify tacks in the 2D window (ver3.1.0).
content_description: The purpose of this webpage is to provide a step-by-step guide for using the Tack function in CLO 3D to visualize fit adjustments by temporarily fixing points on a draped garment.

title: [Property] Flip Topstitch
content: ### Objective Use the Flip function to set a Topstitch on an Internal Shape/Line in a different direction (inside and outside). When setting the Topstitch on the Pattern's cutting line, the Topstitches always appear on the inside of a Garment and the Flip function gets deactivated. **Location** Property Editor ▶ Placement ▶**Flip** **Operation** 1. Select a Topstitch with ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005670908/_________.png) **Edit Topstitch** tool in the 2D window for changing its properties. → Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Placement ▶**Flip** → The Topstitch direction is now being changed.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on using the Flip function to adjust the direction of Topstitches on internal shapes or lines in garment design.

title: Add Block Folders in the Modular Configurator Window
content: **List of Contents** Create Folders Rename Folders Delete Folders Configurator Window Options ### ### **Objective** Create and manage Modular Configurator categories and folders. ** Location** Modular Mode ▶ Vertical Menu Tab on the Left ▶ **Modular** **Configurator** **Operation** **Create Folders** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Vertical Menu Tab on the Left ▶ **Modular** **Configurator** →Modular Configurator window appears. 2. Click on the (**+**) icon at top-right corner of the Configurator. →Open Category window appears. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000603227/Add_Folder_2.png) 3. Select a folder. → The selected folder appears in the Configurator. **Rename Folders** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Vertical Menu Tab on the Left ▶ **Modular** **Configurator** →Modular Configurator window appears. 2. Right click on the tab and click **Rename**. → Rename window appears. 3. Rename folders. **Delete Folders** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Vertical Menu Tab on the Left ▶ **Modular** **Configurator** →Modular Configurator window appears. 2. Right click on the name of the category tab to delete. → The category is now being deleted. **※ Note:** The Block files belong to the according category also gets deleted. **Configurator Window Options** **Update** | Update any changes of the folders. ---|--- **Display** | Change folder file display. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for creating, renaming, and deleting folders within the Modular Configurator to efficiently manage categories.

title: Express Air Pressure
content: ### **Objective** Use the **Pressure** value to create an effect of air or padded materials such as padded jumpers, pillows, cushions, balloons and etc. **Location** Click Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Pressure** **Operation** 1. Select a Pattern to express pressure with ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005592427/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png) **Edit Pattern** or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005592407/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) **Transform Pattern** tools. → Its properties appear in Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Pressure** 3. Adjust the value as desired.
content_description: Learn how to utilize the Pressure value in the Property Editor to simulate realistic air and padded effects in materials like jumpers, pillows, and cushions.

title: Edit Curvature
content: **Objective** Convert a straight line to a curved line or edit a curved line's curvature. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Curvature** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001096687/_______.png) **Edit Curvature** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Curvature** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001096687/_______.png) **Edit Curvature** 2. Click and drag a straight line to convert it to a curved line. → AI Bezier handles are added to the both end of the selected line. 3. Or, click and drag a curved line to edit the curvature.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for converting straight lines to curved lines and editing the curvature of existing curved lines in the 2D Pattern editing tool.
